overview.headline: 16 of the 20 providers in this cycle's queue look unusual even beyond their size, and 7 desk review recommendations need a second look.
overview.summary: We ranked 1082 providers. The top 20 form the queue: 9 for Full audit and 11 for Desk review. 16 of the 20 look unusual beyond their size. Nineteen are hospital and outpatient providers.

actions.why: All 9 Full audit providers look unusual even when size is set aside. Their billing resembles providers previously suspected, so they are the clearest cases to justify to a supervisor.
11 providers are suggested for Desk review. 7 of them look unusual beyond their size, so a Full audit may fit better. Double-check these 7 before you settle on a desk review.

overview.how_to_read: A higher rank means billing looks more like providers previously suspected. It does not show wrongdoing. Large providers can rank high just because they are big. Use the rank to decide where to look first, not what you will find.
watch_out_for: 7 Desk review recommendations look unusual even when size is set aside. Check whether a Full audit is the better choice.
4 of the 20 queue providers do not look unusual beyond their size. Their rank may mostly reflect how large they are.
19 of the 20 queue providers are hospital and outpatient. The queue says little about other types of care.
Of the top 100, 74 were previously flagged, against 69 when sorted by payments alone. The gain over payments alone is small.

caveats.text: A past flag means previously suspected, not proven. A high rank is a reason to look, never a finding.
Large legitimate providers often rank high just because they bill more. Check size before you open a case.
How past flags were assigned is undocumented, so we cannot say how reliable they are.
This uses public, probably synthetic 2008-2009 data, so treat this page as a demonstration.
A person decides. This ranking never denies or delays a payment.

overview.headline: 16 of the 20 providers in this cycle's queue look unusual even after allowing for size, and 7 desk review recommendations need a second look.
overview.summary: We ranked 1082 providers and put 20 in the queue. Of these, 9 are for full audit and 11 for desk review. 16 of the 20 look unusual beyond their size.

actions.why: All 9 full audit providers look unusual even after allowing for size. This is the strongest case for opening a review, but each still needs your own check.
11 providers are suggested for desk review. 7 of them look unusual even when size is set aside, so a desk review may be too light. Look at these 7 again first.

overview.how_to_read: A higher rank means billing looks more like providers previously suspected. It does not show that anything is wrong. Large providers can rank high just for being large. Use the rank to decide where to look first, not as a finding.
watch_out_for: 7 desk review recommendations look unusual beyond size. Consider whether a full audit fits better before you settle on desk review.
19 of the 20 queue providers are hospital and outpatient. The queue says little about outpatient-only providers.
In the top 100, 74 were previously flagged, against 69 when sorted by payments alone. The gain over simple payment size is small.
Providers outside the queue have no recommendation. Being outside it does not mean they were cleared.

caveats.text: A past flag means previously suspected, not proven. A high rank is a reason to look, never a finding of wrongdoing.
Large legitimate providers often rank high just because they bill more. Check the size-adjusted view before you justify a referral.
How past flags were assigned is undocumented, so the ranking may repeat old habits or gaps in earlier reviews.
This uses public, probably synthetic data from 2008 to 2009, so treat this as a demonstration, not real casework.
A person decides what happens next. The ranking never denies or delays a payment.
